protocol.gate: For every window in 30, 60, 100, 250 and 500 bars: median booked Sharpe above 3, absolute median tradable Sharpe below 0.5, and phantom share of booked P&L between 0.9 and 1.1
protocol.question: Do rolling-hedge spread books show a high Sharpe ratio on independent random walks while the P&L of a position that holds the previous hedge stays near zero?

card.ai_assistance: An AI assistant copied the files and wrote the protocol, the reproduce script and this record; the operator reviewed them.
card.baseline_control_summary: Control: the tradable P&L series of the same paths, which holds the previous hedge.
known_limitations: Retrospective record: the study predates this frozen protocol.
card.manual_review: The operator compared the table in the preprint with results.json.
card.public_claim_text: Rolling-hedge spread books look profitable on independent random walks while the tradable P&L is near zero.
card.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Rolling-hedge spread books look profitable on independent random walks while the tradable P&L is near zero.
card.raw_payload_manifest: No raw payload; the simulation generates its own random walks.
card.source_rights_note: Own simulation code and output, MIT licence in the source repository; no third-party data.

body.claim_boundary: Simulated independent random walks only, seed 20261015, 400 paths of 5000 hourly bars. Says nothing about real markets or about any investment result.
